_comment: TIER A — characters and creatures. Group file for:
uv run --project tools/art tools/art/generate.py characters --dry-run
Four entries, four billable calls, producing the art behind 150 emitted sprites
(128 carrier bodies 400..557, 16 corpses 560..575, 6 weapon glyphs 601..606) plus
the camo/glitch/hit-flash overlays that the baker derives from the carrier mask.
Every dimension below is EMITTED WIRE PIXELS AT RS=4 (ART_UPGRADE_PLAN §1).
RS=4, TileSize=6 -> TilePxR=24; BodyW/H=8/12 -> BodyWR x BodyHR = 32 x 48;
CorpseW/H = 2*TilePxR x TilePxR = 48 x 24; weapon glyph 20 x 20 (on the 20px floor).
Registration is the whole game here: code stamps fixed-position marks over the baked
blit, so the crop rect decides whether they land. Target-space anchors, derived from
render.nim bodyPixels/corpsePixels doubled from RS=2 to RS=4:
carrier 32x48 — hull top edge y=10, hull base y=36, hull x-span 4..28 (max half
width 12), crown specular y=8..9. Rows 36..47 are the code-stamped team diamond
(x 10..22, centred x=16) and MUST be empty in the generation. Rows 0..7 are the
2px bob-lift headroom (frame=1 blits at dy=-(RS div 2) = -2) plus margin.
Parity pip is stamped near x=10,y=14 — keep the left shoulder plain.
corpse 48x24 — hull y-span 6..20, hull x-span 6..38, ink top edge y=4..5, dead
visor x 12..24 / y 10..12. Rows/cols x>=38 are the code-stamped spilled diamond
(x 34..42, y 12..20) and MUST be empty in the generation. The alpha shadow pool
stays in code (the key pass binarizes alpha to 0/255, so a soft pool cannot be
generated — §3.4 step 6).
Crop rects live in art/sheets.json, hand-verified by eye against actual_px, never
here and never auto-detected (§3.3). The hard rule: crop.w/target.w == crop.h/target.h
== 2^k, k>=2. Legal rects per family are listed in each entry's notes.
Cell -> sprite index mapping (facing enum is render.nim:187, '0 S, 1 N, 2 E, 3 W'):
carrier-sheet   TL=facing 0 S, TR=facing 1 N, BL=facing 2 E, BR=facing 3 W
weapon-glyphs   TL..TR = iSword, iSpear, iBow; BL..BR = iKnives, iBlowgun, iNet
(items.nim declaration order, so ord() indexes the sheet directly)
Never mix cells across two takes of a sheet. The sheet exists to make the facings
mutually consistent; a hull from take 2 beside a hull from take 1 reintroduces exactly
the per-image drift the sheet was chosen to prevent. Pick one take whole, or re-run.

DECISION 2026-08-18 (world.json header, 'cheapest is also strongest'): weapon-glyphs DROPPED from this group. The six held glyphs are cut as a concentric 320x320 second crop of world/stencil-sheet cells 1-6 (16x -> 20x20), tinted phosphor in code from the same alpha mask — one vocabulary, zero drift, zero extra images. Fallback if the 70% fill reads too light at 1:1: restore this entry re-authored to match stencil-sheet word for word.

defaults.prompt_prefix:
Orthographic elevation, seen dead level and straight on, flat parallel projection.
One key light from the upper left; the ground beneath the subject stays unlit and bare.
The background is one continuous field of pure #00FF00 touching all four edges — the only green in the image.
Every surface is clean and unmarked, pure pictorial artwork.
defaults.prompt_suffix:
The subject will sit on dark slate, RGB(40,48,57) — light it for that.

Palette, four object-bound ramps:
  chassis and structure in desaturated blue-grey #1C242B through #4E5E6B
  live emission in pale cyan phosphor #A5E3EE, highlights #EAF7FA
  matter, loot and energy in warm amber #FFB454, the one warm tone
  ink lines and deep recesses in near-black blue #10161C
Every colour comes from these ramps or the green backdrop.

prompts.name: carrier-sheet-a
prompts.prompt:
A 2 by 2 grid of four views of ONE machine — the same machine four times, turned.
The whole image is a tall rectangle split into two columns and two rows, so each of the
four cells is itself a tall rectangle two units wide by three units tall. The cells are
separated by the bare, continuous #00FF00 background alone, and each machine is centred
in its cell, standing directly on the green field — beneath every base there is only #00FF00.

Reading order, and it must be exactly this:
  top left     — the machine faced straight at the viewer, its sensor band square on
  top right    — the machine faced directly away: its back is unbroken hull carrying a
                 single raised spine ridge down the centre
  bottom left  — the machine turned a quarter turn to the viewer's right: the sensor band
                 slid hard against the right-hand chamfer of the upper block
  bottom right — the machine turned a quarter turn to the viewer's left: the sensor band
                 slid hard against the left-hand chamfer of the upper block
The machine turns; the camera holds still. Every cell is the same level, straight-on
orthographic elevation.

The machine is a TALL, SLENDER carrier — its body twice as tall as it is wide, a narrow upright sliver of a machine: a bilaterally symmetrical chassis whose entire body is
one sealed chamfered machined block of glowing pale cyan phosphor — the hull itself is
the light source, its plates lit #8ACFDC with #A5E3EE where the key light lands standing on its own tucked base — the block is the
whole machine. Every edge is straight and hard-machined, every corner a flat 45-degree
cut: the family's eight-sided block profile, here waisted by one extra chamfered cut into
each flank. Its single feature is a recessed sensor band across the upper third of the
body, near-black #10161C, holding a single small bright pale-cyan pupil — one round pupil, centred, and the band is otherwise empty; everywhere
else the hull is smooth, sealed, featureless plate.

THE SILHOUETTE IS THE DESIGN. This is Chassis A, the slender carrier. Its proportions
are the whole identity: the body stands two full units tall for every one unit of width —
a narrow, upright wafer. Read the outline top to bottom: a slim crown; long shallow
45-degree shoulder chamfers; flanks that pull inward to a marked waist at mid-height,
where a clean wedge of green background bites into each side; a lower block that flares
slightly wider than the shoulders; a quick chamfer into a small tucked base. Beside its
broad teammate it reads like a blade beside an anvil, and the two waist bites of
background are the signature — deep enough to stay visible at final icon size.

It is lit like a phosphor instrument: pale cyan #8ACFDC over most of the hull, #A5E3EE
across the crown where the key light lands, one narrow #EAF7FA specular strip along the
top chamfer, #6EB4C2 on the lit left flank, #3E6B76 on the right flank as it turns away,
#2A4A52 under the tucked base.

All four views share one identical silhouette, proportion, size, position and lighting
direction; between cells the single change is which way the machine faces and where the
sensor band therefore sits. The left-shoulder region stays plain flat hull — a mark is
composited there later.

Inside every cell, exactly: the machine is horizontally centred, its top edge one sixth
of the way down the cell, its base three quarters of the way down, its widest line about
five-eighths of the cell's width. The top sixth and the bottom quarter of every cell hold
only the flat #00FF00 field.

Pixel art, drawn as if on a 128 by 192 pixel grid per cell — exactly four times the final
icon — then shown enlarged: hard-edged square blocks of flat colour aligned to the grid,
each shape one solid fill, every boundary a crisp stair-step.

On this machine the pale cyan phosphor ramp covers every hull plate; the near-black
#10161C appears only in the recessed sensor band and the ink lines between plates;
and the #00FF00 backdrop fills everything outside the silhouette. The hull is a
luminous instrument, clearly brighter than any dark machine casing.

Built to survive reduction to a 32 by 48 pixel icon: bold silhouette, large masses, every
stroke, notch and gap at least one twelfth of the sprite width.
prompts.notes: CHASSIS A = PARITY 0 (bodyPixels parity 0 draws this sheet; parity 1 draws carrier-sheet-b). Target 32x48 per facing (BodyWR x BodyHR at RS=4). 2:3 sheet (~1365x2048) so each 2x2 cell (~682x1024) is itself 2:3 and the top-sixth / bottom-quarter reservation lands. Legal crops: 512x768 (16x, expected) or 256x384 (8x). Place each rect so the hull top edge falls at 1/6 of rect height and the base at 3/4 — registration must be IDENTICAL to carrier-sheet-b, because the code-stamped team diamond (rows 36..47), the frame=1 bob lift, and the pip site are shared by both chassis. Silhouette contract at 32px wide: upper block ~16px, waist ~12px, lower block ~20px (hull x-span within 4..28). Pip site x=10,y=14 falls 2px inside A's upper-block flank — verify on the accepted take before bake. Acceptance test: box-reduce one cell of A and one of B to 32x48 and overlay — A reads ~8px narrower at the shoulder line and both waist notches survive as >=1px bites of background; otherwise re-run. Accept A and B as a pair from takes with matching family language; never mix cells across takes, never mix chassis across mismatched takes. Bake: --size 32x48 --ink stone --emit-mask (per-chassis masks feed glassBodyPixels, glitchPixels, hitFlashPixels).

prompts.notes: CHASSIS B = PARITY 1 (the teammate; the code-stamped shoulder pip stays on this parity as the redundant identity channel — hence the plain left shoulder). Target 32x48 per facing (BodyWR x BodyHR at RS=4). 2:3 sheet (~1365x2048), cells ~682x1024 at 2:3. Legal crops: 512x768 (16x, expected) or 256x384 (8x). prompts.name: corpse-wreck
prompts.prompt:
One wrecked machine, toppled onto its side, lying still and dead.

It is a carrier of the same machined family as the standing chassis, now horizontal — an even slab whose width sits between the two standing silhouettes, committing to neither: one chamfered
block with vertical flanks and 45-degree cut corners, eight-sided profile, hard machined
edges, no curves, no fillets, no head, no limbs, no wheels, no weapon. It has fallen to
the viewer's left, so its sensor end lies at the left and its narrow base points right.

The wreck occupies one horizontal band exactly twice as wide as it is tall, centred in the
frame, with generous empty background above it, below it, and to the right of it. The
rightmost fifth of that band is empty background: the hull stops short of it and nothing
at all is drawn there.

The sensor band is dark and dead — a flat near-black #10161C slot near the left end with
no pupil and no light in it whatsoever.

It is cold and unpowered; every surface is inert plate. Use only the dark end of the phosphor ramp,
#2A4A52 and #3E6B76, with a thin #52909D catch of the key light along the upper flank,
#1C242B to #2A3742 in the recesses, and near-black #10161C as the ink line along the top
edge. The brightest value anywhere on the wreck is that single #52909D catch of key light; every other surface sits darker.
sparks, no fire, no smoke, no blood, no gore, no organic matter. This is a dead machine,
not a body.

Damage reads as structure, not as debris: one flank plate sprung loose along a chamfer,
one corner sheared flat, the base buckled where it hit. No scattered rubble, no dust, no
loose fragments floating clear of the hull, no crater, no cast shadow and no shadow pool
beneath it — the shadow is drawn separately.

Pixel art, drawn as if on a 192 by 96 pixel grid — exactly four times the final icon —
then shown enlarged: hard-edged square blocks of flat colour, no anti-aliasing, no blur,
no soft shading, no gradient inside a shape, no texture noise, no outer glow.

Of the palette below, this image uses ONLY the blue-grey structure ramp, the dark end of
the pale cyan phosphor ramp, and the near-black ink. No amber, no magenta, no red, no
team colour.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 48x24 pixel icon: bold silhouette, large shapes,
no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.
prompts.notes: Target 48x24 (2*TilePxR x TilePxR at RS=4). 16:9 (~2048x1152) is the closest supported ratio to the 2:1 target band; the band sits centred with vertical margin. Legal crops: 1536x768 (32x, expected) or 768x384 (16x). Generate AFTER the carrier sheet is accepted and compare chassis language side by side — this is the one entry that cannot be made consistent by sheeting, so if it reads as a different machine, re-run with the accepted sheet's clauses restated, and if it still drifts, hand-topple the baked carrier instead. The prompt deliberately never says corpse, body or death: it describes a wrecked machine, which both avoids a safety block and is what AFTERGLOW actually wants (§3.5 — the grave marker is the dropped loot, not gore). Bake: --size 48x24 --ink stone. CHASSIS-NEUTRAL: shared by carrier-sheet-a and carrier-sheet-b; hull width sits between the two silhouettes.

prompts.name: camo-shimmer-plate
prompts.prompt:
One flat plate of faceted refractive glass, seen straight on, filling and over-filling the
whole composition. The plate's own edges run past the framing on all four sides, so no edge
of the plate is visible and no background is visible either — the plate IS the background,
edge to edge. It covers the frame completely, so there is nothing for the key colour to key
and no #00FF00 should appear anywhere in this one image.

The material is broken into large flat facets, like a cracked pane or a rough-cut crystal
seen face on: straight-edged shards meeting at hard angles, each facet somewhere between
one sixth and one third of the frame width across, each facet a single plain unshaded fill,
no two adjacent facets the same value. A few facet boundaries catch the upper-left key light
as a bright straight sliver of #C6EDF4 or #EAF7FA; every other facet stays in the dark end
of the phosphor ramp, #2A4A52 through #52909D, with #1C242B in the deepest facets.

It is a material swatch, not an object: no subject, no figure, no silhouette, no machine,
no border, no frame, no vignette, no corner darkening, no repeating tile pattern, no visible
seams, no lens flare, no bloom, no blur, no gradient, no anti-aliasing, no caustics.

Pixel art, drawn as if on a 128 by 192 pixel grid — exactly four times the final icon —
then shown enlarged: hard-edged square blocks of flat colour.

Of the palette below, this image uses ONLY the pale cyan phosphor ramp and the darkest
blue-greys. No amber, no magenta, no red, no team colour.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 32x48 pixel icon: bold silhouette, large shapes,
no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.
prompts.notes: OPTIONAL and OUT OF THE 36-IMAGE BUDGET. The plan puts camo/glitch/hit-flash in Tier B at ZERO images: all three are derived from the baked carrier's alpha mask, because an independently generated silhouette guarantees misregistration (risk #3). This entry does not violate that — it generates a MATERIAL, never a silhouette. The baker masks it with CarrierPose[facing].mask and glassBodyPixels applies its own alpha (rim 96 / fill 30) exactly as today, so registration still comes from the mask and the baked plate stays opaque (0/255 alpha, keeping the §3.4 step-6 histogram assertion valid). Generate only if the mask-derived camo reads as a flat wash at 1:1; the fallback is the pure-code derivation and nothing else changes. The full-bleed instruction contradicts the group prefix's 'background: flat pure #00FF00' on purpose, and harmlessly: if the model surrounds the plate with green anyway, the hand-verified crop takes an interior rect and the surround never reaches the baker. Crop an INTERIOR rect only, never one containing the plate's own edge: 1024x1536 (32x, expected) or 512x768 (16x). Bake: --size 32x48 --palette phosphor --ink none.
